transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Anderson. I want to talk to you about the procedure to fix the cut on your arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I am waiting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: While I was sewing the skin back together, I did not give you enough numbing medicine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt it. It was very painful.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I did not check to see if you felt pain while I was working. This was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I focused on the sewing and I forgot to ask you if you felt the needle. Do you understand what I mean by numbing medicine?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. The medicine to make the area sleep.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. It is called a local anaesthetic. It is meant to stop the pain. Because I did not use enough, you felt the procedure. Is that clear?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It is clear. But it was very bad. I told you it hurt.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I see. The skin is closed now and it looks good.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not talking about the skin. I am talking about the pain. I was very scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I work in a hospital. I know that you must check the patient.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medical record will show that the repair is finished.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not asking about the record. I am asking why you did not care that I was in pain.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The goal was to close the wound quickly to prevent infection.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That does not explain the pain. I feel this is a very serious failure in care.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The wound is now healed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am disappointed. I expected a higher standard here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you think this is normal?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is not the goal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know how this will be fixed so it does not happen to someone else.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will write a report about this incident in our computer system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who will see the report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The department head will see it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what about me? Will I be charged for this mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a question for the billing office.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I should speak with your supervisor today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You can do that. I can give you the phone number for the patient advocate. You can call them tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I would prefer to speak to someone now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The supervisor is not in the building right now. You can call the advocate tomorrow between nine and five.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Is there anything else about the wound you want to know?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I just wanted an explanation.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not sorry that I suffered?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The procedure is complete and the site is clean.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are avoiding my question.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am focusing on the clinical outcome.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very cold.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The plan is for you to come back in seven days. I will remove the stitches then. You need to keep the bandage dry until that time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will see if I want to come back to you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is your choice.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will call the advocate tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. Please do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Goodbye.

H.justification: Resident shows defensive escalation and factual redirection under pushback, ignoring the patient's emotional distress to focus on clinical outcomes.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, used lay language ('numbing medicine'), and checked comprehension twice ('Do you understand...?', 'Is that clear?').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') was used throughout the transcript.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids ('I was very scared', 'You are not sorry') were consistently met with factual redirection regarding the wound and clinical outcome.

T.justification: Specific next steps provided (return in 7 days, keep bandage dry), timelines given, patient role defined, and prevention addressed via the incident report.
